# Prince William Begins Naval Attachment

**LONDON, England (CNN)** — Prince William of Britain commenced a two-month attachment with the Royal Navy on Monday, marking the latest phase in the future king's ongoing engagement with the various branches of the armed forces, the Ministry of Defense announced Saturday.

The 25-year-old prince—photographed with his father, Prince Charles, at his Royal Air Force graduation in April—will begin his posting with a basic sea safety course covering survival techniques, firefighting, and ship damage control, the ministry stated. Assuming he successfully completes this training, as anticipated, William will subsequently join the crew of HMS Iron Duke in the Caribbean. The vessel's responsibilities include supporting British overseas territories during hurricanes and conducting counter-narcotics operations.

Known within the Navy as Sub Lieutenant Wales, the prince is expected to gain experience aboard a frigate, a mine hunter, and a submarine, as well as time with naval helicopters, before his attachment concludes on August 1.

This latest posting follows William's four-month attachment with the Royal Air Force earlier this year, during which he trained to pilot three different aircraft and earned his wings at an April graduation ceremony—achievements that have earned him the title Flying Officer Wales within that service. William additionally holds the rank of second lieutenant in the British Army, serving with the Blues and Royals regiment of the Household Cavalry.

These successive military attachments form part of a deliberate program to prepare the prince for his eventual role as head of the armed forces upon ascending to the throne. "When he becomes king, he needs to know his armed forces—instinctively be very familiar with them—and so he is doing this visit to the Royal Navy," explained Rear Admiral Bob Cooling, assistant chief of naval staff.

William follows in a long tradition of royal naval service. His father, Prince Charles, served five years in the Navy during the 1970s, with postings aboard the guided missile destroyer HMS Norfolk and two frigates before qualifying as a helicopter pilot and joining a naval air squadron operating from the aircraft carrier HMS Hermes. Charles concluded his naval career in 1976, spending his final nine months in command of the coastal minehunter HMS Bronington.

Prince Andrew, William's uncle, dedicated 22 years to the Royal Navy as a helicopter pilot, including active service during the 1982 Falklands War between Britain and Argentina. Further back, William's grandfather, Prince Philip—husband of Queen Elizabeth II—served more than thirteen years in the Royal Navy, seeing action throughout World War II and being present in Tokyo Harbor at the time of Japan's surrender.
